title: Stuff You Should Know July 4th Extravaganza, Part 1: Mom
summary: Live recording at SiriusXM studios in New York of a special "Stuff You Should Know" episode about America, Part 1 of a two-part July 4th extravaganza, with guests from The Daily Show with Jon Stewart (Wyatt Cenac, Hallie Haglin) and The Onion (Joe Randazzo, Joe Garden, Jill Morris). Topics include Plymouth Colony crime and punishments (buggery case of Thomas Granger, stocks, dunking), colonial housing and hearth fires, indentured servants and the slave trade, the Stamp Act and tar and feathering leading to the Revolution, Jefferson drafting the Declaration, the history of the curveball and Mordecai "Three Finger" Brown, the Magnus effect, and an Onion segment on "Unsung American Exports" (Santa Claus, syphilis, raccoons, hip hop). Ends with a plug for part two and the Stuff from the Future video podcast.

segments.title: Live show intro and bathroom banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the live SiriusXM studio recording about America, mention a listener's beer complaint, and introduce the guests from The Daily Show and The Onion.

segments.title: Plymouth Colony crime and the Thomas Granger case
segments.summary: Discussion of the Puritan underbelly of Plymouth Colony with Wyatt Cenac, including the buggery case of Thomas Granger, read from 1631 court records, and colonial punishments such as the stocks and dunking.

segments.title: Colonial housing, fire and hardship
segments.summary: Colonists lived in caves, then crude thatched and mud houses with holes in the roof; fires had to be kept going since matches were scarce; the hosts tie this to hardship and disease.

segments.title: Disease, colonization and indentured servitude
segments.summary: Discussion of disease among Native Americans, Spanish pigs brought by De Soto, indentured servants promised land, and the trade that brought about eleven million Africans to the Americas.

segments.title: Stamp Act, tar and feathering, and the road to revolution
segments.summary: Colonists resented British taxes such as the Stamp Act and quartering of soldiers; tar and feathering of tax collectors is described; most taxes were repealed before the colonists revolted.

segments.title: Declaration of Independence
segments.summary: Hosts note Thomas Jefferson drafted the Declaration of Independence in about seven days and joke about writing their own declarations.

segments.title: History of the curveball and Mordecai Three Finger Brown
segments.summary: Chuck explains Mordecai Peter Centennial Brown, who lost fingers in a feed chopper accident and developed a topspin curveball; discussion of the Magnus effect, early skew balls, and whether the curveball is an optical illusion.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Brief transition and sponsor-style break between segments.

segments.title: Unsung American Exports (Onion segment)
segments.summary: Joe Garden and Jill Morris present satirical 'exports': Santa Claus traced from St. Nicholas and Sinterklaas, syphilis origins and the French pox, raccoons introduced to Germany, and hip hop's spread from the Bronx.

segments.title: Part one sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts say this is the end of part one, promote part two and the Stuff from the Future video podcast.
